subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should externally or plugin-registered recurring model-backed cron jobs remain enabled by default, or require explicit operator activation/confirmation with model and cost guardrails?
rationale: The source-reproduced behavior is real, but the fix changes security posture, plugin scheduling semantics, defaults, and upgrade behavior for existing background automation.

options.title: Require explicit activation
options.body: Default non-operator/plugin recurring agent-turn cron jobs to disabled or confirmation-gated, show doctor/update diffs, and require an explicit model or safe cron model default before they run.

options.title: Keep enabled with stronger guards
options.body: Preserve auto-enable behavior only if model-backed recurring jobs must declare safe model/cost policy and billing/auth/quota failures pause them with user-visible alerts.

options.title: Document current trust model
options.body: Keep current auto-enable semantics as trusted operator/plugin behavior and close the issue after documenting the cost and security expectations.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation
recommendation.body: Default non-operator/plugin recurring agent-turn cron jobs to disabled or confirmation-gated, show doctor/update diffs, and require an explicit model or safe cron model default before they run.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central source lines are carried by Vincent Koc's recent refactor commit, and that path spans plugin scheduling, cron defaults, and model selection.
